title: P112: prove the full-group floor for uniformly two-port factors
body:
## Result

Every rational strict fit of the fixed P112 full-group mask has invoice at least **334** if all query columns touch at most two scalar ports. The transpose gives the same floor when all reader rows are two-port. This covers arbitrary fitting rank, term count and dependent factors. It also applies when one common invertible within-group similarity makes an entire factor family two-sparse.

The new step is to allow **permitted free endpoint entries to change**. Independent active query sets are gain trees, grounded trees or unbalanced unicycles. Generic characteristic-two gains retain cyclic/grounded recovery. A tree can recover the required diagonal together with one allowed free entry. All forbidden zeros remain zero, query supports are preserved and actual reader supports shrink. Every resulting strict fit expands to I334, forcing the complete physical-group invoice.

The package separately retains exact-endpoint transfer results and the all-reader seven-query bridge consequence. It also derives a useful necessary screen: an invoice at most 296 needs at least 38 units of overhead under every partition of its dense queries into two-port pieces.

## Validation

Both registered, standard-library Python 3.12 commands pass. Separate implementations authenticate the two scientific inputs, check all 111,556 symbolic strict-fit expansion positions, all 28 free group pairs/420 scalar free entries, exact finite-field and changed-free controls, the residual query's 6+1 refinement, and bridge kernel/reader identities.

The quantified theorem is a written proof with separate AI-agent audits; the programs check its literal premises and controls, not a formal proof kernel. Metadata, committed bytes, source history and official export all pass at `bf5b25241f36643b57c96bb0d0f6990031a66324`. Both scientific commands also pass from a fresh read-only Git-free export with empty PATH; all 15 exported files remain unchanged (0.36 seconds, Python 3.12.14 on Windows).

Reproduce: `python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-sparse-gain-transfer`.

## Limits and provenance

This does not prove an unrestricted 334 floor, produce a cheaper decoder, or improve the selected bound. A saving must escape both uniform sparsity conditions; dense queries and dense readers need not occur in the same term. Native execution, restoration, storage, precision and supplier obligations remain open.

Canonical main was refreshed before submission and remains `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244`, priority revision 7. The 20 October overlap snapshot covered 354 open PRs; persistent HTTP 406 prevented fresh Discussion coverage. README distinguishes the projectively-TU, graphic-interface and non-Fano boundary predecessors and retains their credit.

Prepared by flyingviper with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance and independent AI-agent checks. Standard gain-graph facts are credited and proved in the scope needed here. No independent human review or worldwide novelty is claimed. Apache-2.0.
